correctness.rationale: For squarefree semiprime pq the k-hyperperfect condition becomes pq=1+k(p+q), hence (p-k)(q-k)=k²+1 with positive factors. For p<q, let d=p-k, so 1<=d<=k; this bijectively parametrizes candidates with q=k+(k²+1)/d. An independent sieve enumerated p in (k,2k], tested primality of p and integer q=(kp+1)/(p-k) for all 1<=k<=132. Nonzero layers exactly 1,2,6,12,18,30,48,60,66,78,108,132. Double layers only 12 and18; k132 has precisely pairs (137,3617),(157,829),(173,557). Thus finite numerical theorem is correct.

Every solution with 1<=k<=132 satisfies p<=2k and q<=k²+k+1, hence pq<=2*132*(132²+132+1)=4,635,048 <10^11. The published full census therefore exhaustively covers ALL possible lower-index solutions; filtering its k-column yields exactly the submitted least-triple cutoff and double layers. This is covered by an exact database/table even absent identical theorem wording. The failing originality assessment is based on positive decisive coverage, not a failed search or access limitation.
